page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.medium is a general-purpose instance powered by a single dedicated AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 core running at 3.3 GHz. The server features 4.0 GB of system memory, a 48 MB L3 cache, and a bundled 59 GB NVMe SSD local instance store volume. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance in specific tasks, with top-tier results in gzip compression at 36.23 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.04 GB/sec. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores are low. Memory bandwidth is mixed, showing average performance on large-block reads at 42.93 GB/sec but poor results on small-block reads and large-block writes.

The instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for ARM64 development and lightweight workloads, combining dedicated CPU allocation with high-speed local NVMe storage. The primary tradeoff is the single-core limitation, which restricts multi-threaded scaling and limits database operations and static web serving throughput to lower performance tiers.

This server is suited for lightweight general-purpose applications, single-threaded data processing tasks like compression and decompression, microservices, and development or testing environments requiring local SSD storage.
